clue.text: Councillor's gutted by Oxford's river disaster

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, so only the outer letters of the councillor survive

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A local councillor is devastated by some calamity on the river in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' in the wordplay: Councillor, gutted to CR, is placed by ISIS. 'gutted' reads as upset but is the instruction to empty the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a moment of acute trouble or calamity, close in meaning to a disaster.

clue.text: Eggs, when split by line, part

indicators.note: being split by something means having it wedged into the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs in a fish

explanation.surface: Some eggs, once a line divides them, separate into parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' is a noun here, as in an actor's part.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the character an actor plays, which is also called a part.

clue.text: Old whaler's work: capturing felons in Wash, possibly

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one piece surrounds the other
possibly signals that the letters of Wash may be arranged another way

parts.note: crims is informal shorthand for criminals, that is felons

explanation.surface: An old whaling craft seized some convicts in the Wash, the bay on England's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash' looks like the bay, a large inlet on England's east coast, but is just anagram fodder signalled by 'possibly'; 'capturing' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw is carving or engraving on whalebone or ivory, done by sailors on old whaling voyages.

clue.text: Wearing the blue turned up, duck? Figure-hugging!

indicators.note: the sky is wearing the other piece, meaning it is wrapped around it

parts.note: the blue is a poetic name for the sky

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for duck is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so nil

explanation.surface: Someone in blue, flipped upside down like a duck diving, shows off a tight outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses in this down clue and 'Wearing' encloses. A duck is a cricket score of zero; 'the blue' is a poetic name for the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A slinky dress clings closely to the body, so it is figure-hugging.

clue.text: Moved — not natural

definitions.meaning: ... also means artificial or put on for show

explanation.surface: Stirred emotionally, though in a manner that seems put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being affected is both being emotionally stirred and behaving in a pretentious, artificial way.

clue.text: Immediately when Derby, say, fell

definitions.meaning: the phrase is an idiom meaning instantly, without hesitation
a derby is a bowler hat, so a hat falling is literally the drop of a hat

explanation.surface: Something happened instantly the moment a Derby went down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' reads as the horse race or the city, but here it is the bowler hat Americans call a derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at the drop of a hat means doing it straight away, without needing any encouragement.

clue.text: European region's loud people being grounded

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
landers are those who land, coming down to the ground

explanation.surface: Noisy people in some part of Europe are being kept on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is a historic region of north-west Europe, now largely in Belgium.

clue.text: In public, a romantic American's billiards shot

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is held within the run of words that follows, across their joins

explanation.surface: An American who makes a romantic gesture openly also plays a good billiards shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside 'public, a romantic', where the letters run across the word breaks. Carom is the American word for a cannon in billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: A carom is a billiards shot where the cue ball strikes two balls in turn, the American term.

clue.text: State means to create a fast road

parts.note: to state something is to express it
a way is a means or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A government's method for building a quick road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun, a political body, but it is the verb to express.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressway is a high-speed divided highway, a road built for fast traffic.

clue.text: Tending to scare off star Liam

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A famous Liam has a tendency to frighten people away.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist spreads needless fear, so alarmist talk tends to scare people.

clue.text: Truncated fancy bra raised temperature

indicators.note: fancy suggests something elaborated or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: raised means up, lifted higher

explanation.surface: A short, elaborate bra pushed up gets someone hot under the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrupt is cut short suddenly, which is what truncated describes.

clue.text: Live within one's means, as a contortionist could

definitions.meaning: to earn just enough to cover one's spending
a contortionist can literally bend so that both ends of the body touch

explanation.surface: A frugal lifestyle, likened to the bendy feats of a circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Making ends meet is the idiom for managing to live on one's income without debt.

clue.text: Move of bishop to China, not a fate that's rectified

indicators.note: something rectified is put right, so these letters are set into their proper order
not a means the letter a is dropped from the word China

explanation.surface: A churchman relocates to China, sparing himself an unhappy destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' turns China into CHIN; 'rectified' rearranges TO + CHIN + FATE. Fianchetto is a chess opening term.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a fianchetto develops a bishop to the long diagonal, a specific bishop move.

clue.text: Essential element of Depression: onset of hunger

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so take its first letter

explanation.surface: Hunger setting in was a core feature of the Great Depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests the 1930s slump but is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith of something is its core, the essential part of an argument or matter.

clue.text: High earners taking in southern mountain air quality

indicators.note: taking in means admitting something inside, so one piece goes within the other
high as in drunk or intoxicated suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Top-paid workers in the south enjoy the quality of fresh alpine air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' anagrams EARNERS to RARENES and 'taking in' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Air at altitude is thin, having less oxygen per breath, and that thinness is its rareness.

clue.text: Meadow saffron for the Coventry horsewoman?

definitions.meaning: a folk name for the autumn crocus, which flowers without leaves
Lady Godiva rode naked through the streets of Coventry, according to legend

explanation.surface: A wild flower is named for the famous rider of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva, by legend, rode naked on horseback through Coventry, an English city, to protest her husband's taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadow saffron is popularly called naked lady since its flowers appear without any leaves.

clue.text: One who's been caught arriving with drugs in need of support

parts.note: arr is the timetable abbreviation for arriving
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so ES is several such pills
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A captured person showed up carrying narcotics and needing help.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrestee is a person who has been taken into custody by the police.

clue.text: Son with present (sweet flower)

parts.note: now is the present moment
a drop is a small boiled sweet, like a lemon drop

explanation.surface: A son gives a gift of candy and a pretty bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but it is the time now.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white flower of late winter.

clue.text: Break small piece off end of thick raised surface

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth such as velvet

explanation.surface: Chipping a fragment from the edge of a thick, rough surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To knap is to chip flint or stone, striking off small flakes.

clue.text: Newspaper possibly reveals 'Goddess married to heartless youth'

parts.note: Hera was queen of the Greek gods

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline exposes a goddess's marriage to a cold young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle A from LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Herald is a common newspaper title, as in the Glasgow Herald, a messenger of news.

clue.text: East Midlands town doctor set child free

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: In a Midlands town a physician releases a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun, a physician, but is a verb meaning to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield is a market town in Derbyshire, in the East Midlands of England, noted for its crooked spire.

clue.text: Proust's character is weak, going in opposite directions

indicators.note: going in means entering, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: south and north are opposite compass points, S and N
wan means pale and feeble

explanation.surface: A Proust figure is feeble and pulled two ways at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Swann is a leading figure in Proust's novel In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: You once cut many hundreds

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the end of the word is chopped off

parts.note: ten hundreds make a thousand

explanation.surface: Long ago you sliced through hundreds of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic second-person pronoun, meaning you in older English.

clue.text: Royal house's beginning to encompass university

indicators.note: to encompass something is to enclose it, so one piece is put around the other

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: A dynasty's founding included setting up a university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were the dynasty ruling Scotland and later England, a royal family line.

clue.text: Bother an educator and an iconic rebel

parts.note: a head is a head teacher, the senior educator in a school
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, is famous from a widely copied portrait

explanation.surface: A teacher and a famous revolutionary are causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache, figuratively, is a nuisance or source of worry.

clue.text: Feathers are better than a baton movement

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathers of a bird
to beat a rival is to be better than them

explanation.surface: Feathers outdo a conductor's stick in some contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A downbeat is the conductor's downward stroke marking the first beat of a bar.

clue.text: Uninteresting ladder trial

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting
a ladder in tights is a run, a line of snagged stitches

explanation.surface: A dull test of a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British word for a run in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal, a practice trial before the real thing.
